title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an access-control failure inside a law enforcement deployment. A licensed user of a camera network and of criminal justice databases is accused of running queries for a personal purpose, against a person with no investigative connection to him. The systems performed as designed: they returned location and record data to someone holding valid credentials. Nothing in the reported facts describes a model error, a false output, or a system operating outside its intended technical conditions. The failure sits in the gap between who is authorised to query and what the query is for.

The searches are alleged to have occurred across 2024 and 2025, and the conduct is alleged to have continued over years, which places the detection problem after the fact rather than at the point of use. Catching this kind of misuse requires logging that ties each query to a case or purpose, review that compares queries against the officer's assigned work, and alerts on repeated lookups of one individual by someone with no reason to look. A camera network that answers a plate or location query cannot by itself distinguish policing from stalking.

What is not established is whether Rogers committed a crime or violated policy: the department filed a complaint and opened an internal affairs investigation, and a complaint is not a finding. The restraining order is a civil protection, not a criminal conviction, and the Select Board has not yet voted on his employment.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of misusing police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended the relationship about five years ago, changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits after leaving. She discovered this summer that Rogers had searched for her location using the Flock camera system and other law enforcement databases, including CJIS and CORI, multiple times in 2024 and 2025. She also said he drove by her home.

The Stow Police Department filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 and placed him on paid administrative leave in July, then unpaid leave as of July 31. The department found his conduct unbecoming of an officer after a four-week internal affairs investigation. The woman has obtained a restraining order lasting at least a year. A Select Board hearing is scheduled next week, when town leaders could vote on Rogers' employment status.
